title: Helping Customers When You Don't Know the Answer
short_description: Learn how to respond with confidence when a customer asks an unfamiliar question. Gather details, verify information, and make a helpful handoff.
learning_objectives: Respond professionally when you do not know an answer.
Gather the information needed to research a customer question.
Check the best available source before giving technical advice.
Connect the customer with the right person and share what you learned.
Recognize questions that need a manager, manufacturer, or qualified professional.

lessons.title: Stay Calm and Take Ownership
lessons.learning_objective: Respond professionally when you do not know an answer.
lessons.why_this_matters: Customers expect help. They do not expect every new employee to know everything.

content_sections.heading: Be honest and helpful
paragraphs: Say you want to verify the answer. Keep a calm tone. Avoid guessing or dismissing the customer.

content_sections.heading: Own the next step
paragraphs: Explain what you will do next. You might check a label, consult a coworker, or find official instructions.

content_sections.heading: Stay connected
paragraphs: Do not send a customer away without a clear handoff. If you must leave, explain where you are going and return as promised.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer asks whether a certain blade fits their saw. You are unsure. You say you will check the saw model and blade information before giving an answer.
what_to_say_or_do: Say: “I want to make sure we get this right.”
Ask for the product model or package.
Explain the next step.
Return with an answer or a clear referral.
common_mistakes: Saying “I don’t know” and walking away.
Promising an answer you cannot verify.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask a specialist when product compatibility or safe use is uncertain. Never recommend an unverified blade or accessory.
key_takeaways: Take responsibility for the next step.

unscored_practice.question: You do not know whether a blade fits a saw. What should you say?

choices.C: “Let’s check the model and the blade specifications.”

unscored_practice.explanation: Checking the model and specifications is a useful next step. It avoids guessing.

lessons.title: Ask Questions That Find the Missing Detail
lessons.learning_objective: Gather the information needed to research a customer question.
lessons.why_this_matters: Many questions are hard to answer because key details are missing.

content_sections.heading: Clarify the problem
paragraphs: Ask what the customer is trying to do. Find out what is not working or what needs replacing.

content_sections.heading: Identify the product
paragraphs: Ask for a model number, measurements, old part, package, or photo. Do not assume similar-looking parts are interchangeable.

content_sections.heading: Repeat the request
paragraphs: Summarize what you know. This helps the customer correct missing or misunderstood details.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer needs a replacement filter but does not know the size. You ask for the equipment model and the label on the old filter. You can now look for a verified match.
what_to_say_or_do: Ask: “What equipment is this for?”
Ask: “Do you have the model number?”
Ask: “Can you show me the old part or a photo?”
Repeat the key details.
common_mistakes: Asking for details unrelated to the problem.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask a coworker for help identifying a model or part. Use manufacturer documentation for compatibility.

unscored_practice.question: A customer needs a filter but does not know the size. What detail would help most?

choices.B: The equipment model or old filter label.
choices.C: The date of their last store visit.

unscored_practice.explanation: A model or filter label can help verify compatibility.

lessons.title: Use Reliable Information
lessons.learning_objective: Check the best available source before giving technical advice.
lessons.why_this_matters: A confident guess can lead to a wrong purchase or unsafe use.

content_sections.heading: Start with the product
paragraphs: Read the package and labels. Look for model numbers, sizes, ratings, and warnings. Do not treat packaging as a substitute for full instructions when more detail is needed.

content_sections.heading: Use official instructions
paragraphs: For compatibility, safety, and warranty questions, prefer current manufacturer information. Check that the document matches the exact model.

content_sections.heading: Know what is not confirmed
paragraphs: If you cannot verify a claim, tell the customer. Explain the next safe step.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer asks whether a particular battery works with a power tool. You compare the exact tool and battery models using official compatibility information. You do not rely on color or appearance.
what_to_say_or_do: Say: “Let’s check the model information.”
Read the label with the customer.
Use current official product instructions when available.
State clearly what remains unverified.
common_mistakes: Relying on memory for a safety claim.
Using instructions for a different model.
Treating an online comment as a manufacturer policy.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask a specialist or manager if official information is unavailable or unclear. Refer the customer to manufacturer support or a qualified professional when appropriate.
key_takeaways: Do not present guesses as facts.

unscored_practice.question: A customer asks whether a battery fits a tool. Which source is strongest?

choices.A: A guess based on the color.
choices.B: A comment from an unknown forum.
choices.C: Current manufacturer compatibility information for the exact models.
choices.D: A similar product on the next shelf.

unscored_practice.explanation: Official information for the exact models is more reliable than appearance or guesses.

lessons.title: Make a Helpful Handoff
lessons.learning_objective: Connect the customer with the right person and share what you learned.
lessons.why_this_matters: A customer should not need to repeat the same story several times.

content_sections.heading: Choose the right helper
paragraphs: Find a coworker with relevant product knowledge. Use a manager for store policy or an unresolved service issue.

content_sections.heading: Summarize the need
paragraphs: Tell the next employee what the customer wants, what details you checked, and what remains unanswered.

content_sections.heading: Follow through
paragraphs: Confirm that the handoff happened. If no one is available, explain the options without promising a time you cannot guarantee.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer needs a part for a pressure washer. You have the model number but cannot confirm the fitting. You introduce the customer to the power equipment specialist and share the model number and the question.
what_to_say_or_do: Say: “I have the model number. Let me bring in our equipment specialist.”
Share the details already collected.
Confirm the customer knows who will help next.
Avoid promising a wait time without checking.
common_mistakes: Making the customer repeat every detail.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Ask a manager when a specialist is unavailable or a customer needs a policy decision. Refer technical work beyond retail advice to a qualified professional.

unscored_practice.question: You need to transfer a customer to a plumbing specialist. What should you do?

choices.A: Tell the customer to find someone in plumbing.
choices.B: Introduce the specialist and share the details you already gathered.
choices.D: Give an answer you are unsure about.

unscored_practice.explanation: A good handoff saves time and shows ownership of the customer’s need.

lessons.title: Know When to Stop and Escalate
lessons.learning_objective: Recognize questions that need a manager, manufacturer, or qualified professional.
lessons.why_this_matters: Some questions involve risks or decisions outside a retail employee’s authority.

content_sections.heading: Recognize higher-risk topics
paragraphs: Electrical wiring, gas connections, structural loads, chemical mixing, and power equipment safety can involve serious hazards. Product advice is not a substitute for professional work.

content_sections.heading: Separate product facts from professional advice
paragraphs: You may help locate a product or find official instructions. Do not design, approve, or certify work that requires a qualified professional.

content_sections.heading: Escalate clearly
paragraphs: Explain why you need another source. Ask a manager for store policies. Use official manufacturer support for unresolved product questions. Recommend a qualified professional for work beyond your role.

lessons.hardware_store_example: A customer asks you to confirm that a fastener will support a heavy overhead load. You can help find product specifications. You do not approve the installation. You explain that the load and installation need qualified evaluation.
what_to_say_or_do: Say: “I can help find the product specifications.”
Say: “I cannot confirm this installation is safe.”
Refer to a qualified professional for technical approval.
Ask a manager about store policy.
common_mistakes: Treating a package rating as approval for every installation.
Giving installation advice outside your training.
Ignoring a warning because a customer wants a quick answer.
lessons.when_to_ask_for_help: Escalate immediately when there is a safety concern, an unclear manufacturer warning, or a request for technical approval outside retail scope.

unscored_practice.question: A customer asks you to approve hardware for a heavy overhead installation. What should you do?

choices.C: Find product specifications and refer the installation decision to a qualified professional.
choices.D: Tell the customer any fastener will work.

unscored_practice.explanation: Retail employees can provide verified product facts. They should not certify a high-risk installation.

questions.learning_objective_assessed: Respond professionally when you do not know an answer.
questions.question: A customer asks a question about a product you have never sold. What should you do first?

choices.A: Guess based on the product name.
choices.B: Say you will verify the information and explain the next step.

questions.explanation: Honesty and a clear next step build trust. Guessing or dismissing the customer does not help.

questions.learning_objective_assessed: Gather the information needed to research a customer question.
questions.question: A customer needs a replacement part for a tool. Which information is most useful?

choices.A: The tool model number and old part details.
choices.C: The color of the store sign.
choices.D: The day the customer usually shops.

questions.explanation: Exact model and part details support a reliable match. The other details do not identify the part.

questions.learning_objective_assessed: Check the best available source before giving technical advice.
questions.question: A customer asks about a tool battery’s compatibility. What is the best next step?

choices.A: Choose one with the same color.
choices.D: Check current manufacturer information for the exact tool and battery models.

questions.explanation: Manufacturer compatibility information for exact models is the appropriate source. Appearance and unrelated manuals are not reliable.

questions.learning_objective_assessed: Connect the customer with the right person and share what you learned.
questions.question: You have collected a pressure washer model number but need help finding a fitting. How should you hand off the customer?

choices.B: Tell them to start the story over.
choices.C: Introduce a specialist and share the model and unanswered question.
choices.D: Leave without confirming anyone is available.

questions.explanation: A direct handoff with the known details saves time and keeps the customer supported.

questions.learning_objective_assessed: Recognize questions that need a manager, manufacturer, or qualified professional.
questions.question: A customer asks you to approve a fastener for a heavy overhead load. What is the best response?

choices.A: Promise it is safe if the package shows a high rating.
choices.B: Help locate specifications and refer the installation decision to a qualified professional.
choices.D: Say you can certify the installation.

questions.explanation: Product ratings do not establish suitability for every installation. A qualified professional must evaluate the application.
